chapter_note: This chapter is predominantly a compact cosmological-cosmic stability teaching (three "rocks" fixed into the universe). The second-half pastoral drift is localized in ¶5, where the third rock is redefined as a support of the "holy church"—an institutional application that breaks the cosmos→cosmos mapping and reads like an editorial extension of the otherwise systematic triad.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame incipit (hagiographic/editorial container): "Once again he speaks to his disciples:"

paragraphs.core_text: Three great rocks, which exist, were appointed by the greatness. They were set in these outer worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural statement establishing a numbered triad fixed into cosmic geography; no audience address, citation, or institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the first rock is the [Pillar] of Glory, the Perfect Man, which was summoned [by the] glorious Ambassador. He set it in this zone; [ ... he] brought forth its base (?) from the earth to heaven. It bore up under the [en]tire uni[verse], and became first of all the weight-carriers in [it]s powers. In its firmness it has been set upright, and has made fast every [t]hing above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological exposition: named cosmic beings (Perfect Man, Ambassador) and cosmic mechanics (bearing up the universe; fixing above/below) in an impersonal descriptive voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second great and glorious rock is the new earth of light, which was set upon the earth of Darkness. It has squashed the fastenings of the five storehouses of Death. It has established firmness, with great firmness, over and beyond the earth of Darkness. It has flattened, crushed and fixed the root of Death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos mapping continues: light/dark earths, storehouses, and Death as a cosmic principle. No pivot into church practice or exhortation.

Editorial application: the triad is extended/redirected into an institutional referent ("holy church"), shifting from cosmic emplacement to community anchoring. Even if "Jesus, the glorious one" can be a cosmological figure, the decisive marker is the cosmos→church identification.

paragraphs.core_text: [These] are the three great rocks, they that have come forth in great confidence, in three great and honoured places. They were appointed and distributed in three great places of these [self]same worlds. They were made fast according to the will of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative recapitulation in the same impersonal, distributive-cosmic register (three places in the worlds), without institutional or citation language.
